sources.title: Biological waste treatment: appropriate measures for permitted facilities
sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance covers aerobic and anaerobic biowaste facilities and appropriate measures for permitted operations.
sources.guard: Treat sector guidance and process scope as regulatory evidence only; require observed quantity, unit, period and verified geometry before parcel GHG promotion.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: when appropriate measures apply
sources.fact: The guidance covers composting, anaerobic digestion, methane collection and biomethane upgrading, while BAT conclusions inform permit conditions.
sources.guard: Do not convert BAT applicability, AD scope or biomethane process descriptions into measured methane or parcel greenhouse-gas values.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: general management appropriate measures
sources.fact: Operators must maintain management systems, emission inventories, monitoring schedules and relevant risk-management plans.
sources.guard: Management-system requirements, inventories and maintenance records are control evidence, not direct emissions measurements.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: waste pre-acceptance, acceptance and tracking
sources.fact: The guidance requires waste-stream knowledge, acceptance procedures and tracking before biological treatment.
sources.guard: Waste identity, composition, tonnage or tracking status must not be promoted to GHG without compatible activity-to-emission methodology and scope.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: waste treatment
sources.fact: Facilities must identify and characterise process emissions and use process monitoring and control systems.
sources.guard: Process controls and design parameters are not observed release quantities; preserve measurement versus operating-condition boundaries.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: outputs
sources.fact: Operators record treatment outputs, residues, weights and dispatch information.
sources.guard: Output tonnage and residue records are activity data; do not equate them with emitted GHG without a compatible verified conversion chain.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: emissions control
sources.fact: The guidance covers emission inventories, monitoring requirements, point and fugitive emissions, abatement and BAT-associated emission levels.
sources.guard: Keep emission limits, inventories, abatement systems and monitoring requirements separate from actual validated concentration, flow, duration and mass results.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: process efficiency
sources.fact: Operators monitor annual water, energy, raw-material, residue and wastewater use and maintain energy-efficiency plans where applicable.
sources.guard: Resource use and energy-efficiency indicators are not absolute GHG without compatible activity data, factor vintage and scope.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: site location, design and capacity
sources.fact: The guidance addresses sensitive receptors, fugitive emissions and site design/capacity considerations.
sources.guard: Site location, capacity and receptor proximity are spatial/risk evidence; they do not establish measured emissions or cadastral attribution.

sources.title: Biological waste treatment: waste storage, segregation, transfer and handling
sources.fact: Facilities must manage storage capacity, segregation, handling and containment under permit limits.
sources.guard: Storage capacity and handling controls are operational evidence only; do not infer emissions magnitude from their presence.

sources.title: Intensive farming risk assessment for your environmental permit
sources.fact: Updated 1 May 2026, the guidance covers ammonia screening, emission factors and detailed assessment for intensive farming permits.
sources.guard: Ammonia screening factors and predicted impacts are model inputs/results, not measured GHG or parcel observations.

sources.title: Request an ammonia screening assessment
sources.fact: Published 1 May 2026, the Environment Agency requires screening before relevant new or varied intensive-farming permit applications.
sources.guard: Screening requests and outcomes are permitting evidence; do not promote them to measured emissions.

sources.title: Landfill methane: measurement and metrics
sources.fact: Published 2 February 2026, this Environment Agency project assesses methods for measuring landfill methane emissions and their potential regulatory use.
sources.guard: Research-method capability and study conclusions are not site-specific measurements unless an explicit measured result, method, uncertainty and site scope are present.

sources.title: Monitoring landfill gas surface emissions: LFTGN 07
sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance covers walkover surveys, flux-box quantification, interpretation and reporting for landfill surface methane emissions.
sources.guard: Monitoring procedure and compliance framework must stay separate from actual survey observations and quantified flux results.

sources.title: Control and monitor emissions for your environmental permit
sources.fact: Updated 3 December 2025, the guidance explains permit emission controls, monitoring needs and use of accredited monitoring systems.
sources.guard: Permit conditions, monitoring obligations and MCERTS requirements establish quality/control context, not the emission value itself.

sources.title: Non-hazardous and inert waste: emissions monitoring and limits
sources.fact: Environment Agency guidance links emission limits and monitoring requirements to process, emissions inventory and environmental risk assessment.
sources.guard: Emission inventories and permit limits must not be treated as observed annual GHG or parcel measurements.

sources.title: Monitoring stack emissions: environmental permits
sources.fact: The collection links Environment Agency monitoring strategy, periodic-monitoring and continuous-monitoring standards, including documents updated in 2026.
sources.guard: Monitoring standards and method hierarchy are provenance/quality requirements; require validated measurements for emissions claims.

sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance: Monitoring and Reporting Regulation 2018
sources.fact: Published 6 August 2025 and updated 5 May 2026, the collection covers UK ETS monitoring, uncertainty, biomass, data flows, sampling and waste MRV.
sources.guard: Monitoring plans, uncertainty rules and reporting methodologies are accounting controls; they do not themselves prove a facility or parcel emission amount.

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme: technical guidance and tools
sources.fact: Updated 26 June 2026, the collection provides technical guidance, emission factors and reporting templates for UK ETS operators.
sources.guard: Scheme factors/templates are calculation inputs; require correct activity data, reporting period, installation scope and verified mapping before any parcel-level claim.

sources.title: Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026
sources.fact: Published 11 June 2026, the government factors support calculation and reporting of 2026 Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions from activity data.
sources.guard: Conversion factors alone are not emissions observations; require compatible 2026 activity data, units, scope and provenance and never infer parcel ownership or geometry.
